blocks.label: Raise power for each free follow-up hit in a row
blocks.summary: While my free follow-up move is queued, its power is multiplied by 1 plus 0.1 for each hit in a row. Example: after 3 hits in a row, power x1.3.
blocks.whenLabel: While the game calculates a move's power

params.label: Extra power per hit in a row (0.1 = 10%)

feasibility: Only while my free follow-up is waiting to resolve (the streak is armed)
The bonus is 10% of the power for each hit in a row that landed so far
blocks.packageReason: The 10% step is a constructor argument (default 0.1) and an editable param. The marker name perpetual-motion is deliberately NOT a param: it is the shared key that ties this attr to the follow-up move and to four other attrs of the same ability (three of them in B17); changing it on this attr alone would silently switch the bonus off, and the gate is the editable slot for the condition. Package, reason: the multiplier is `1 + streak x 0.1` where the streak is a per-Pokemon counter written by PerpetualMotionProgressAbAttr; effect.multiply-power only takes a fixed number (a counter-based power effect is requested). Users (1): Perpetual Motion (6022) attr 4 of 5. Gate is legacy-closure pending move.scripted-marker. The armed-state check stays a non-editable guard clause in the class (it is state of the ability's own machine, listed under feasibility, not a registered guard). Oddities, not fixed: canApply does not call super.canApply, so skipDuringMovesetGen is ignored (it is false for this class, so no effect); the class applies on simulated power previews too, which is correct for damage previews.

blocks.label: Count free follow-up hits that land in a row
blocks.summary: After my free follow-up move, I count one more hit in a row if it hurt the target, or reset the count to zero if it did not.
examples: Count each free Rollout that lands in a row so the next one hits harder
feasibility: Only counts a follow-up that is still waiting for its result (the streak is armed); a hit that did not hurt the target resets the streak
Does nothing while the game is only previewing a hit
blocks.packageReason: Package, reason: the effect is one step of a counter state machine (pending flag and streak) shared with PerpetualMotionTriggerAbAttr, PerpetualMotionPostTurnAbAttr, PerpetualMotionResolutionAbAttr (B17) and PerpetualMotionPowerAbAttr; the library has no counter effect (requested). Users (1): Perpetual Motion (6022) attr 3 of 5. Gate is legacy-closure pending the request move.scripted-marker. Oddities, not fixed: the inherited attackCondition (`move.category !== STATUS`, constructor argument 0) is not exposed as its own slot; for this user it is always the default, and the gate re-states it as move.damaging. The streak is stored on summonData, so it resets when the Pokemon leaves the field.

blocks.label: Gain an extra type when I enter
blocks.summary: When I enter the battle, I gain the Electric type in addition to my own types. Example: a Water type that gains Electric becomes Water and Electric.
examples: Gain the Electric type when I enter the battle
feasibility: Does nothing if I already have that type
The new type lasts until I leave the field
blocks.packageReason: The gained type is a constructor argument (default Electric, so the shipped ability is unchanged) and an editable param. Package, reason: no effect.add-type in the effect library (requested), not because the effect cannot be split. Users (1): Photovoltaic (6030) attr 1; attr 0 is a SelfHighestStatMultiplierAbAttr (Solar Power half) from another batch. apply writes pokemon.summonData.types, which is reset when the Pokemon leaves the field. It ignores `simulated` (never read), harmless because PostSummon is never dispatched simulated. A Pokemon that already has summonData.types set (a type change before entry) keeps that list and gets Electric appended; with no summon types it starts from getTypes().

feasibility: There must be a foe still standing
No delayed attack may already be waiting on that foe's position
Nothing is set up while the game is only previewing
blocks.packageReason: The attack list and the delay are constructor arguments (defaults Future Sight and Doom Desire, 3 turns, so the shipped ability is unchanged) and editable params. Package, reason: no delayed-attack effect in the library (requested); the class itself is one call to positionalTagManager.addTag with fixed arguments (sourceMoves [Future Sight, Doom Desire], turnCount 3), so it should be re-declared as an event-effect with params {moves, turns} when the effect exists. Users (1): Prophetic (6014) attr 0 (its only attr). Oddities, not fixed: canApply is the inherited true, so the ability flyout can show when no delayed attack is set (no foe, or a delayed attack already waiting on that slot); the tag is aimed at the first living foe only, never at both foes in a double battle.

blocks.label: Re-aim queued attacks at the next foe after my punch
blocks.summary: After my punching move hits, every move still queued this turn that aims at a foe is re-aimed at the next foe over. Example: with two foes, the targets swap.
examples: After a punch hits, the foes' targets are shifted one slot to the right
feasibility: The move must really have hurt the target (it dealt damage and was not blocked), and the game must not be only previewing
I must still have this ability active
There must be at least two foes on the field to rotate between
blocks.packageReason: Package, reason: the effect rewrites `battle.turnCommands[*].targets` and `command.move.targets` for every queued command; no library effect touches the turn queue (requested as effect.rotate-queued-targets). Users (1): Southern Cross Punch (6016) attr 0 (its only attr). Gate legacy-closure pending move.has-own-flag; the guards need not-simulated and hit-dealt-damage (requested). The inherited attackCondition (constructor argument 0, default `move.category !== STATUS`) is never read: this canApply does not call super. Oddities, not fixed: (1) the class rewrites commands that already executed this turn as well as later ones, harmless but wider than the description 'later intended targets'; (2) the rotation also re-aims the holder's own queued command and its ally's; (3) clause 5 is redundant for the shipped ability.
